标题: 1 dead , 2 firefighters injured as blaze engulfs Atlantic building in Mumbai
正文(前2500字): MUMBAI: A 64-year-old man died and two firefighters were hospitalised after a fire broke out on the seventh floor of Atlantic Building on Sherly Rajan Road in Bandra West late on Wednesday night. The fire, which was brought under control close to midnight, had initially triggered fears of people being trapped inside the building. According to the Mumbai Fire Brigade (MFB), the incident was reported at 9.12 pm and was upgraded to a Level-I fire at 9.55 pm. The blaze was extinguished at 11.50 pm after an intensive firefighting operation involving fire brigade personnel, police, 108 ambulance services, Adani Electricity staff and ward officials. The fire was spread accross to electrical wiring, electrical installations and household articles in Rooms 701 and 702 on the seventh floor of the ground-plus-seven-storey building. During the operation, reports emerged of persons stranded on the top floor, leading firefighters to launch search and rescue efforts. Civic authorities later confirmed that Azim Barodawala (64) was brought dead to Bhabha Hospital. Two firefighters also sustained injuries while battling the blaze. Shivshankar Bharat Puri (32), attached to Bandra Fire Station, and Navnath Mohan Bite (34) were admitted to Bhabha Hospital after suffering suffocation during the operation. Earlier in the night, local residents said the flames spread rapidly across the top floor, creating panic in the neighbourhood. The fire was visible from several nearby high-rise buildings as multiple fire engines worked to prevent it from spreading further. The exact cause of the fire remains unknown.

标题: Dead woman found in burning Bronx building

正文(前2500字): An acrid smell of smoke hung thick in the air surrounding the former Boston & Maine Signal Tower on Monday morning. Firefighters were dispatched on Sunday evening to extinguish a fire at the abandoned 800-square-foot structure, which sits at the bottom of an unkempt wrap-around stairway beneath the Water Street bridge. The historic building between the gasholder and Route 3 has been left vacant since 1985. The Concord Fire Department received a call about a building fire at the former signal tower at 10:23 p.m. on Sunday. Firefighters arrived three minutes later to meet Concord Police officers, according to a fire incident report. Firefighters entered through an above-ground basement door and contained the fire to the basement as heavy smoke filled the first floor. The fire was “knocked down” within ten minutes of firefighters’ arrival. The building, now charred from the inside out, was an integral part of Concord’s rail yard during the early 20th-century. It was acquired by rail giant CSX Transportation in 2022. At the time, CSX had “pledged to invest over $100 million into upgrades,” according to a statement by the New Hampshire Historic Preservation Alliance on Monday. Three years later, the structure remained unrestored and was occupied by groups of unhoused individuals. Concord Fire Prevention is conducting an ongoing investigation to determine the cause of the fire. There were no reported casualties. Brendilou Armstrong can be reached at barmstrong@cmonitor.com

正文(前2500字): SEOUL, Oct. 21 (Xinhua) -- No casualties were reported Tuesday in a high-rise building fire in South Korea's capital Seoul, which led to the evacuation of more than 100 people, according to Yonhap news agency. The fire broke out at the 16-storey building near Seoul Plaza in front of the Seoul City Hall at around 9:46 a.m. local time (0046 GMT). The blaze was contained about 44 minutes later, with no casualties found from the building, which had been under renovation. A total of 104 workers who were remodeling fled the building, while three received emergency care. Some 10 construction workers, who failed to evacuate due to heavy fumes, were waiting for rescue at the rooftop. Fire authorities estimated that the fire started from the third floor of the building, planning to investigate the exact cause of the accident. ■

Six charges were filed against Hausman, including first-degree felonies of Arson, Inhabited Building; Aggravated Arson, Bodily Injury; Arson, Danger of Death or Bodily Injury; third-degree felonies of Risking Catastrophe and Criminal Mischief; and a second-degree misdemeanor of Recklessly Endangering Another Person. All four Tamaqua Fire Companies responded to the fire incident that was reported around 12:42 p.m. Wednesday, when callers reportedly saw flames coming from the 9-unit apartment building located at 44 Mauch Chunk St. Tamaqua EMS and Police, and Coaldale Fire Department also responded to the scene. Upon arriving, fire personnel found an active fire and rescued Hausman, a tenant, from a second-floor window via a ladder. Police say Hausman admitted to starting the fire on purpose, after being evaluated by EMS. Hausman was taken to St. Luke’s Miners Hospital in Coaldale for smoke inhalation and other injuries, where police say she is still receiving care. A 62-year-old female tenant was also rescued — an EMT carried the woman, who uses a walker, out of the building. Besides a second EMT who received onsite care for smoke inhalation, no other injuries were reported. Later in the day, Tamaqua Police and the State Police Fire Marshal discovered remnants of a shower curtain within the fire area. Officials determined that the fire originated along a wall in the suspect’s unit and spread throughout the apartment. Police say damage was contained to the apartment unit that the fire originated in, thanks to emergency responders’ timely response. Apartment residents were permitted to return to their homes later in the day, after the building was deemed safe and secure.

标题: Five hospitalized after apartment fire at Sheridan Ridge complex

OVERLAND PARK, Kan. (KCTV) - Five people were hospitalized after a fire at the Sheridan Ridge Apartments early Saturday morning. Firefighters from Overland Park, Lenexa and Shawnee fire departments were dispatched to the building fire at 83rd and Farley Street shortly before 3 a.m., the Overland Park Fire Department said. According to OPFD, the first units on the scene reported smoke and fire showing from a two-story apartment building with victims on the roof. Officials said firefighters rescued two victims from the roof, while crews located two additional victims in a second-story bathroom and brought them out through a window. One additional victim was found on the ground outside the apartment. One adult and three children were transported to area hospitals in critical condition, and one adult was transported in stable condition, OPFD said. Crews brought the fire under control in about 15 minutes and did not spread to other apartments. No additional injuries were reported by OPFD, and the cause of the fire is under investigation. 标题: Fire inside walls of Roswell apartment building displaces 17 residents
正文(前2500字): ROSWELL, GA — A fire that spread through the walls of a Roswell apartment building left several units damaged and displaced 17 residents. Roswell Fire and Rescue says crews arrived at the complex on Ashley Forest Drive, off Nesbitt Ferry Road, to find only light smoke coming from the building. Firefighters quickly discovered hidden flames moving through wall spaces between apartment units and worked through the night to open the walls and stop the fire from spreading. Several apartments sustained significant fire, smoke, and water damage. No one was critically hurt, though one firefighter from a neighboring agency suffered a minor injury. A cat was also safely rescued and returned to its owner. The Red Cross is now assisting 17 displaced residents. Roswell Fire officials say the incident serves as an important reminder to check smoke detectors and have an emergency action plan, especially heading into the holiday season. WSB Radio’s Veronica Waters contributed to this story.
